short: Self-healing polymer coatings of polyurea-urethane/epoxy ble
title: Self-healing polymer coatings of polyurea-urethane/epoxy blends with reversible and dynamic bonds

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Self-healing FTPU coatings heal well but lack adhesion and hardness as coating materials. BMI Diels-Alder crosslinking of furan epoxy oligomers should phase-separate epoxy domains in FTPU and tune coating properties.
states.detail: Absorbed: p1 (HYP/need), p2 (HYP/hypothesis), p3 (DES/base_system), p4 (DES/modification), p5 (DES/variable_sweep), p6 (PRC/synthesis), p7 (PRC/synthesis), p13 (PRC/stimulus). Premises: Earlier FTPU/epoxy blend work [41] without furan end groups; Disulfide exchange and urea hydrogen bonding make polyurethanes self-healing [42,43]

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Stoichiometric-BMI blends contain crosslinking-induced phase-separated epoxy domains dispersed in FTPU, more at 5:5. At 130 C retro-DA regenerates furan and maleimide groups; at 60 C DA re-forms the adduct, reversibly over cycles.
states.detail: Absorbed: p8 (STR/microstructure/distribution), p14 (STR/chemistry/bonding), p15 (STR/microstructure/distribution). Premises: In AFM phase images bright = hard domains, dark = soft domains; 1146 cm-1 band = furan ring; 696 cm-1 band = maleimide; Furan-maleimide Diels-Alder adducts dissociate (retro-DA) near 110-130 C and re-form at ~60 C; Blend transmittance rises when domains become miscible because light scattering drops

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: DA-bonded nanoscale crosslinked epoxy domains act as hard phase restricting FTPU chain mobility and carrying load. Tensile strength rises from ~7.8 MPa (FTPU) to ~14.3 (FT7BE3) and ~15.3 MPa (FT5BE5).
states.detail: Absorbed: p10 (MEC/pathway), p11 (PRP/value), p12 (PRP/value), p16 (MEC/pathway), p17 (PRP/value). Premises: Furan-maleimide Diels-Alder adducts dissociate (retro-DA) near 110-130 C and re-form at ~60 C

states.title: Performance state
states.head: After hot-press healing, blend coatings on wood and tinplate block pigment staining and saline corrosion

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Reversible DA-crosslinked epoxy domains strengthen and harden FTPU coatings while keeping thermally triggered self-healing and anticorrosion

nodes.title: MICRO, F2, F3
nodes.head: FTPU fracture surface smooth with a clear crack path; blend surfaces rough and granular, FT5B0.5E5 smoother than FT5BE5. FT5B0.5E5: low-contrast protrusions in height (e) and dark isolated domains in bright matrix in phase (j), inverse of FT5BE5
nodes.solves: Stoichiometric-BMI blends contain crosslinking-induced phase-separated epoxy domains dispersed in FTPU, more at 5:5
nodes.necessity_reason: p8 keeps shown support from o2, o7 after removal.

nodes.title: SEM, F8
nodes.head: SEM after 130 C quench: smooth featureless surface, unlike rough F2c. SEM after 130 C then 60 C for 2 h: surface still smooth, no granular domains
nodes.solves: Retro-DA dissolves the epoxy domains into FTPU at 130 C; they do not re-form on cooling to 60 C
nodes.necessity_reason: p15 keeps shown support from o21 after removal.

nodes.solves: DA-bonded nanoscale crosslinked epoxy domains act as hard phase restricting FTPU chain mobility and carrying load

nodes.note: text says 'evident Tg peak at ~63 C' for FT7BE3; image shows a shoulder rather than a resolved peak; FTPU low peak at ~-30 C (text -25 C)

nodes.title: MECH:hardness, F4
nodes.head: Radar: blends and epoxy score well above FTPU in adhesion and pencil hardness; all equal on flexibility

nodes.note: FT7BE3 (red) trace not visible, presumably under FT5BE5 (blue); FT5B0.5E5 slightly lower in adhesion/hardness than FT5BE5

nodes.title: evidence, F5
nodes.head: Healed vs original curves: FTPU and FT5BE5 recover most (FT5BE5 healed stress >= original); FT7BE3 loses most elongation (~77 vs ~112%)
nodes.solves: FT5BE5 retains high healing efficiency (R_H 80.4%) close to FTPU (86.5%); FT7BE3 and low-BMI blend lower
nodes.detail: o11: Healed vs original curves: FTPU and FT5BE5 recover most (FT5BE5 healed stress >= original); FT7BE3 loses most elongation (~77 vs ~112%)

nodes.title: MECH:scratch, F7
nodes.head: Scratch width narrows sharply after brief heating (row 2) and cracks are nearly gone after longer heating (row 3)
nodes.solves: Healing = shape-memory crack closure at 130 C, then repair by retro-DA chain mixing, disulfide exchange and DA re-bonding
nodes.note: faint residual crack traces remain in g and i
nodes.detail: o16: Scratch width narrows sharply after brief heating (row 2) and cracks are nearly gone after longer heating (row 3)
nodes.necessity_reason: p16 keeps shown support from o15 after removal.

nodes.title: ASSAY:stain, MECH:scratch, F6
nodes.head: Unhealed scratched coatings: red stain along wood scratches and corrosion/undercutting on tinplates. After healing and the same exposure, FT5BE5 and FT5B0.5E5 wood and tinplate panels stay largely free of stain and corrosion.
nodes.solves: After hot-press healing, blend coatings on wood and tinplate block pigment staining and saline corrosion
nodes.note: panel label 'Contaminated and corroded coatings' is repeated over F6d as a step label; the reading is from pixels
nodes.detail: o12: Unhealed scratched coatings: red stain along wood scratches and corrosion/undercutting on tinplates; o13: After healing and the same exposure, FT5BE5 and FT5B0.5E5 wood and tinplate panels stay largely free of stain and corrosion; o14: After healing, FTPU and epoxy wood panels still show red streaks and FT7BE3 tinplate keeps light corrosion patches
